clue.text: I use up almost all of income to become this?

definitions.text: I use up almost all of income to become this?

indicators.note: the letters are to become something else, so they are rearranged into the word sought
almost all of the word income means its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone who spends nearly everything they earn wonders whether they will end up penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of I USE UP plus INCOM (income without its last letter, 'almost all of') are rearranged ('to become'); the whole clue also describes how one ends up broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Using up nearly all one's earnings leaves one penniless, which is exactly what the word for poverty-stricken describes.

clue.text: Combine gallons in lake

indicators.note: in says the gallons letter goes inside the word for lake

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond

explanation.surface: An instruction to pour gallons of something into a lake so they mix.
explanation.definitionFit: To combine two things is to blend or join them into one, a synonym.

clue.text: Learned of criminal EU tried

indicators.note: criminal suggests these letters are crooked, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A legal report on a criminal case heard by the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned (pronounced as two syllables) means scholarly or well-read, a synonym.

clue.text: Shaky relative with heart lost to sharp pain

indicators.note: the middle letter of the relative is lost and replaced by the sharp pain

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
a stab is a sudden sharp pain

explanation.surface: A trembling relative whose heart gave way to a sudden sharp pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shaky is wobbly and insecure, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Work briefly to depose, seizing power

indicators.note: seizing means the shortened word grabs the power letter and holds it inside
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to oust is to depose a ruler

explanation.surface: A short account of a coup in which rulers are deposed and power seized.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary work, the Latin word for work.

clue.text: Playful eccentric tips over

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A playful, eccentric person who topples things over.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportive means frolicsome or playful, a synonym.

clue.text: My handler may well be following a lead

definitions.text: My handler may well be following a lead

parts.words: My handler may well be following a lead
parts.note: the speaker is an animal walked on a lead by a handler, who follows the lead in both senses: the leash and a clue in an investigation

explanation.surface: Someone describing their boss, who is chasing up a promising lead.
explanation.walkthrough: A lead is both a leash and a line of inquiry: the dog's handler holds one end and, as a police officer, pursues the other kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine trained to work with officers has a handler who walks it on a leash and also pursues investigative clues.

clue.text: Soldier on exercise eyes invader

indicators.note: exercise suggests the letters are put through their paces and so moved around

explanation.surface: A soldier on a training exercise keeps watch for an invader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' looks like a noun in a military scene, but 'Soldier on' is the definition, an instruction to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exhortations to persevere and refuse to give up whatever the difficulty.

clue.text: Snag with energy enquiry

parts.note: prob is a short form of problem, a snag
E is the abbreviation for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A tricky snag in an investigation into energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A probe is an investigation or inquiry, as in a police probe.

clue.text: Two reports of actual wedding preparation

indicators.note: reports means words heard spoken, and two of them run together sound like the answer

parts.note: actual gives two words, true and so (as in 'is that so?'), both meaning real, said one after the other

explanation.surface: Two news stories about a real wedding being prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: Two synonyms of 'actual', TRUE and SO, spoken together sound like the French word for a bride's outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride gathers ahead of her marriage, so it is part of getting ready.

clue.text: Public facility heading off druggie with bad habit

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a user is a drug-taker
a vice is a bad habit

explanation.surface: A drug addict with a bad habit leaving a public facility.
explanation.definitionFit: A service, such as a bus route or a utility, is something provided for the public.

clue.text: Shunning relations like brothers and sisters?

definitions.text: Shunning relations like brothers and sisters?

parts.words: Shunning relations like brothers and sisters?
parts.note: relations is sexual relations, and brothers and sisters are monks and nuns, who forgo them

explanation.surface: Someone who avoids family members such as siblings.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests siblings shunning relatives; really it is religious brothers and sisters abstaining from sexual relations.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks and nuns take vows to abstain from sex, so they live without intimate relations.

clue.text: Cosmetic ingredient from Chanel, say, possessor of touching property

parts.note: Coco Chanel, the French fashion designer
an abutter is the owner of land that abuts, or touches, a neighbouring property

explanation.surface: A beauty product made by Chanel whose ingredient feels nice to the touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa butter is a fat from cacao beans widely used in skin creams and lotions.

clue.text: Revise book to represent upturns: it's going out …

indicators.note: upturns in a down clue means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to edit is to revise
to be is to represent, as in 'this will be the hero'

explanation.surface: An editor revising a book that is meant to portray economic upturns, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 16 Down. 'upturns' reverses EDIT B BE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The ebb is the falling tide, the sea going out from the shore.

clue.text: Commerce functions subsumed by public transport

indicators.note: subsumed by means the functions are taken inside the vehicle's name

parts.note: a bus is public transport
sines are trigonometric functions

explanation.surface: Commercial functions being taken over by the public transport sector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'functions' looks like events or roles; it is the mathematical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Business is trade and commercial dealing, a synonym of commerce.

clue.text: Fright's not the first worry

indicators.note: not the first means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a scare is a fright

explanation.surface: Reassurance that this fright is not the first worry one has had.
explanation.definitionFit: Care can mean anxiety or concern, as in 'without a care in the world'.

clue.text: … which is this, technically a downturn

definitions.text: … which is this, technically a downturn

parts.words: which is this, technically a downturn
parts.note: the tide going out is a retreat of the water, and technically an economic downturn of two quarters of shrinking output has the same name

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: something going out is technically a downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: Following on from 13 Down, an ebbing tide is a withdrawal of water; economists formally call a downturn by the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a withdrawal or receding, like a falling tide, and a formal economic contraction.

clue.text: City address's first in attempt to establish home

indicators.note: in says the opening letter goes inside the word for settling down

parts.note: to settle is to set up home somewhere

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word address

explanation.surface: Someone trying to set up home in a city whose first concern is the address.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is the largest city in Washington State in the US.

clue.text: Society has a high opinion of ethical pioneer

parts.note: to rate someone is to think highly of them

explanation.surface: A society that greatly admires a pioneer of ethics.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian philosopher is regarded as the founder of Western moral philosophy, a pioneer of the subject.

clue.text: Brute standing on turtle's shell split into layers

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the second
standing in a down clue means the word is set upright, reading upwards

parts.note: a brute is an animal

indicators.note: shell means the outer letters of the word turtle

explanation.surface: A brute standing on a turtle's shell, which cracks into layers.
explanation.definitionFit: To laminate can mean to separate into thin sheets or plates, as well as to build from them.

clue.text: Returning without leader, saw mercy!

indicators.note: returning means the remaining letters are read backwards
without leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a saw is a proverb or adage

explanation.surface: Someone coming back without their leader, crying out for mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' is the noun meaning a saying, not the tool or the past of see.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned exclamations of surprise, as in 'mercy me!'.

clue.text: Welsh river brought up on verges of Spanish one? Raising it may show surprise

indicators.note: on verges of means the reversed Welsh river sits around the edges of the Spanish one
brought up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: the Wye rises in Wales
the Ebro is a river in Spain

explanation.surface: A geography question about one river reaching the banks of a Spanish river, then a hint about raising it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to river, so 'Spanish one' is a Spanish river.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting the arch of hair above the eye is a common facial sign of astonishment.

clue.text: Having lost blood externally, pain faded

indicators.note: externally means the first piece goes around the outside of the second

parts.note: bled means having lost blood
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A patient who has lost blood from an external wound, the pain fading.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleached means whitened or faded in colour, as by sun or chemicals.

clue.text: Show English immorality centred on illicit meeting-place

indicators.note: centred on means the meeting-place sits in the middle of the immorality

parts.note: vice is immorality
a den is a hideout for illicit activity, as in a den of thieves

explanation.surface: A show about English vice centred on a seedy meeting-place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a noun, a performance; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To evidence something is to demonstrate or display it, so the verb is a synonym of show.

clue.text: Cold-hot sickness?

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
H is the tap abbreviation for hot
ill can be a noun meaning a sickness or ailment

explanation.surface: A question about an illness that makes one swing between cold and hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A feverish cold with shivering is called by this name, an illness alternating cold and hot.

clue.text: Extra water source included in rent

indicators.note: included in means the water source goes inside the word for rent

parts.note: rent as past tense of rend means tore
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A landlord charging extra for the water supply as part of the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' is not a payment but the past tense of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left over, beyond what is needed, is surplus or extra, as in 'time in hand'.

clue.text: By way of illustration of Parisian's mounting keenness

indicators.note: mounting in a down clue means the letters climb upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for 'for example'
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A description of a Parisian's growing enthusiasm, by way of illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: Edge can mean sharpness or intensity, as in an edge to one's appetite, a sense of keenness.

clue.text: Car oiled ineptly by oil worker

indicators.note: ineptly suggests clumsy handling, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: by as in multiplication, three by four, is the sign X

explanation.surface: A car badly lubricated by someone working on an oil rig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oil worker' suggests a rig hand; it is a painter who worked in oils.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene Delacroix was a French Romantic painter whose great canvases were in oils.

clue.text: Produce some Sarajevo kerbstones

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Bosnian kerbs in Sarajevo producing something.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a response is to call it forth or bring it about.

clue.text: Book mostly in stages, having got a plane back

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: stepped means arranged in stages

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: flown means having travelled by plane

explanation.surface: A book read mostly in stages by someone who has taken a plane home.
explanation.definitionFit: Steppenwolf is the 1927 novel by Hermann Hesse.
